title: Qt: Fix conversation dialog timeline graph columns
description:
Remove the separate copy of the conversation column type
enum in ConversationDialog. It doesn't correspond to the
enum in ATapDataModel, because it doesn't include the
Conversation ID and Total columns.

Delegates set to the Traffic Tree (a QTreeView) apply to
the displayed column number, not the what is displayed
in the column. That is, when columns are hidden (filtered),
the delegates stay with the old column number and end up
being displayed on new content. That's not what we want;
we want to always have the timeline graph on the Start and
Duration columns. Moving around the Delegate depending on
which columns are filtered is complicated; just set the
TimeLine delegate to the entire TrafficTree, and use the
default paint if we're on any column other than Start or
Duration. This does mean that we don't need to store a
map of Delegates.

Use a slightly different way to get TimelineDelegate to
paint the rect with no text using the current style, so
we can use the default paint with text for other columns.

The timeline graph needs to get the value of the Start and
Duration columns as filtered by the proxy column, so have
the model pass in indices so that they can be mapped to
the current displayed column.

Have the timeline graph apply to just the Start or just the
Duration column if only one is visible.

Together these compute the proper pixel values to apply
the timeline graph to the Start and Duration columns regardless
of which columns are displayed and which are filtered, in any
tab, regardless of what optional columns appear in that tab.

Fix #18860

notes.body:
added 18 commits
  • 6e78a369...f4e9b9d4 - 17 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • e0fb3cf2 - Qt: Fix conversation dialog timeline graph columns
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9819/diffs?diff_id=608182602&start_sha=6e78a3691513496b65ef2ebcba6dc4d4abd31af8)

Usually we do not explitly check against nullptr, just if it exists. Nothing wrong with this here, but if this check fails, we should NEVER just return, but call the parent method ::paint (as done below). Same as in line 49 above, where I seem to have forgotten it as well.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9819/diffs?diff_id=609300069&start_sha=e0fb3cf2bbdbdf709601321a9eb24f2e42437edf#b8be1ffb98f474a64d75a62a464f317adf68c09e_52_49)

That check is unnecessary, because it would also fail for the line above. If the index is invalid, index.data() will return an empty QVariant in any case, making the rest of the code invalid, as it would be handling unknown information.

Also QStyledItemDelegate::paint() is only called on valid indeces, as it will only handle display of data. If the index is not valid, there is nothing to be displayed, therefore ::paint will not be called.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9819/diffs?diff_id=609300069&start_sha=e0fb3cf2bbdbdf709601321a9eb24f2e42437edf#b8be1ffb98f474a64d75a62a464f317adf68c09e_46_46)

In general, besides the smaller issue, the change will work. But, it breaks behavior from a Qt POV. In Qt, if you talk about columns or rows and if you manipulate columns or rows, you do not talk about indeces. Therefore removing the integer and moving to a QModelIndex is breaking behavior. Also, down the line, it might introduce bigger issues, as we might introduce handling which is not depending on rows present. In such a case, the code fails. 

Although it fixes the issue, I would prefer not implementing this solution.

> Therefore removing the integer and moving to a QModelIndex is breaking behavior.

The problem is I don't see a good way to convert from the column number in the model for Start and Duration to the column number currently displayed / accepted by the ProxyModel.

I would have liked to use `QSortFilterProxyModel::sibling`, but that does not map from the column numbers in the source column, but uses the column number as displayed in the proxy.

Something like:
```
QModelIndex indexStart = proxy->mapFromSource(proxy->sourceModel()->index(0, span_px.colStart));
```

does work, though it's doing the same thing just in the delegate code.

I don't think this would ever be called without a row, because `paint` is only called on valid indices, though another option is having a mapFromSourceColumn() function in the proxy (and having it be public) analogous to the one that maps to the source columns.

I not so much have an issue with it being called within paint. I have an issue with changing the public API of the class header to reflect the indeces. Thinking in API terms, that should only reflect the column. 

I do get the issue here though. Let me take a look if I can come up with a solution and we discuss it. I am not sure if I have the time today, but until the end of the week I should have one.

OK, I changed it back to only passing the columns and calling it within paint. That does make more sense in the Qt POV. I reckon that does preserve the behavior in case any other callers later ever use the `TIMELINE_DATA` role but don't need to actually use the column number.
